title: Now the Shades of Night Are Gone
description: Now the Shades of Night Are Gone in Tonic Solfa to HEINLEIN, doh is F: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 3 verses and a piano.
about: These words were printed without an author's name in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion, compiled by Samuel Longfellow and Samuel Johnson (Boston, 1848), as hymn 363, “Morning Hymn”, where the book credits them to Episcopal Collection.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Sevens (7.7.7.7) (7.7.7.7), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to HEINLEIN; any other Sevens (7.7.7.7) tune fits them as well.
underlay: Now the shades of night are gone; Now the morn-ing light is come: Lord, may we be Thine to day; Drive the shades of sin a-way.

lines: Now the shades of night are gone;
Now the morning light is come:
Lord, may we be Thine to-day;
Drive the shades of sin away.
Fill our souls with heavenly light,
Banish doubt, and clear our sight;
May we stand, and watch, and pray.
Save us from our foes around;
Keep us safe from every sin.

source: A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848)
licence: Public domain: anonymous words in print by 1848.
credits: Words anonymous, public domain, as printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848); set to HEINLEIN by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
